summary: Triaged 5 papers. Top result: Scalable Oversight of AI Systems via Recursive Reward Modeling

claims.claim_text: We propose recursive reward modeling (RRM), where AI assistants help humans evaluate other AI systems by breaking complex evaluations into simpler sub-evaluations.
We demonstrate that RRM scales to tasks where direct human evaluation becomes unreliable.
Our results suggest that recursive decomposition is a promising direction for maintaining human oversight as AI capabilities grow.
We propose Constitutional AI, a method for training AI assistants that are both helpful and harmless.
We demonstrate that this approach significantly reduces harmful outputs while maintaining helpfulness.
We present a novel approach to transformer-based language modeling that reduces parameter count by 40% while maintaining performance on standard benchmarks.
We demonstrate that up to 60% of attention heads in large transformer models are redundant for downstream tasks.
We find that CoT reasoning improves performance on arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning tasks by an average of 15-30% across model scales.
We propose a taxonomy of CoT failures and suggest directions for more robust reasoning architectures, including external verification mechanisms and iterative refinement loops.
